description: An interactive fill-in observation table for Grade 7 Science (NCERT Chapter 3, Activity 3.6, Table 3.1). Students select whether an incandescent lamp glows or does not glow for each of six different cell-lamp arrangements, then receive instant feedback with explanations.
subject: Science
chapter: Chapter 3 — Electricity: Circuits and their Components

arrangements.description: Array of 6 arrangement objects representing the different ways to connect a cell and lamp

description.description: Text describing the arrangement of cell and lamp

default.description: Both terminals of the lamp connected to both terminals of the cell via wires
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → one terminal of lamp; Wire from −ve terminal of cell → other terminal of lamp
default.explanation: Both terminals are properly connected. A complete path exists for current to flow through the filament.

default.description: Both wires from cell connected to the same terminal of the lamp
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → metal tip of lamp; Wire from −ve terminal of cell → metal tip of lamp (same terminal)
default.explanation: Both wires connect to the same terminal. Current cannot pass through the filament — there is no complete path.

default.description: Only one wire connected (from cell to lamp), other wire disconnected
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → one terminal of lamp; −ve terminal of cell left unconnected
default.explanation: Only one wire is connected. The circuit is incomplete — current needs a complete loop to flow.

default.description: Both wires from cell connected to the metal case (same terminal) of the lamp
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → metal case of lamp; Wire from −ve terminal of cell → metal case of lamp
default.explanation: Both wires connect to the same terminal (metal case). No current flows through the filament.

default.description: Wires from both terminals of cell connected, but one wire touches the glass (not the terminal)
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → metal tip; Wire from −ve terminal of cell → glass bulb (not a terminal)
default.explanation: Glass is an insulator. The wire touching the glass does not make electrical contact — the circuit is incomplete.

default.description: Lamp terminals connected to cell terminals (reversed polarity compared to arrangement 1)
default.detail: Wire from +ve terminal of cell → other terminal of lamp; Wire from −ve terminal of cell → first terminal of lamp
default.explanation: Both terminals are properly connected forming a complete path. For incandescent lamps, the polarity does not matter!

teaching_notes: Activate AFTER students have seen the six arrangements image (Table 3.1 in the textbook) and ideally tried the physical experiment. Let students fill in independently. After submission, discuss the pattern: 'Only arrangements 1 and 6 work — both have a COMPLETE path.' This builds the foundation for defining an electrical circuit (Section 3.2.5). The key takeaway is that a lamp glows only when there is a complete, unbroken path from one terminal of the cell through the filament to the other terminal.
instructions_for_student: For each arrangement, select whether the lamp GLOWS or DOES NOT GLOW. Think: is there a complete path for current? Fill in all six rows!
learning_objectives: Identify that a lamp glows only when both terminals are connected to form a complete circuit
Understand that connecting both wires to the same terminal does not make the lamp glow
Recognise that an incomplete circuit prevents current flow
Learn that polarity does not matter for incandescent lamps
Build foundation for the concept of an electrical circuit
